# Successive edition diffs

These directories are generated by `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m byz.diff`
(`src/byz/curate/diff.py`). Do not edit them by hand; rerun the command after
a source or converter change.

Each `<left>--<right>/` directory compares two curated editions:

| Directory | Comparison |
| --- | --- |
| `rp2005--rp2005-2019` | official 2005 -> released 2005+2019 |
| `rp2005-2019--rp2018` | released 2005+2019 -> official 2018 |
| `rp2018--rp2018-2023` | official 2018 -> released 2018+2023 |
| `rp2005--rp2018` | official 2005 -> official 2018 |

## Files

- `report.md` - Unicode-first human-readable report.
  `Main-text changes (derived text differs)` lists the verses whose normalised
  Unicode text changes, with the Text word diff first and the Beta-code Source
  second; at an `apparatus-code` entry the Text block is labelled derived and a
  tag line states the source-tier change. `Apparatus-only changes` compacts the
  remaining source-tier differences into one entry per verse, showing the
  Unicode Apparatus word diff first and the Beta-code diff second; an
  `apparatus-code` entry starts with the same tag line, and an entry whose only
  change is Beta-code encoding says so instead of printing an empty diff. The
  per-pair category table carries a Meaning column. The Text diff is normalised:
  paragraph markers, apostrophe typography, and whitespace are omitted.
- `changes.csv` - one row per source-tier difference, with the category, the
  Beta-code source word diff, the Unicode Text word diff (`text_word_diff`),
  the Unicode Apparatus word diff (`apparatus_word_diff`), the full left/right
  source and exact text, and the `text_changed` and `apparatus_changed` flags.
  The `category` value is the source-tier classification (see Categories
  below); the word diffs are normalised and `text_left`/`text_right` are exact.
- `source.diff` - word-diff style, one line per verse, for the Beta-code
  source tier.
- `text.diff` - word-diff style, one line per verse, for the exact Unicode
  accented main text. It includes every source-differing verse whose exact text
  differs, including formatting-only changes such as a `¶` edit.
  Paragraph markers and apostrophes are shown as stored.
- `apparatus.diff` - the word diff of the normalised Unicode accented text with
  variants (`csv/accented/with-variants`) for every apparatus-only change that
  has a Unicode difference (encoding-only rows are named in `report.md`).
  Variant readings stay inside `{...}` braces, and the braces are literal text
  inside the diff markers. `source.diff` is the Beta-code view of the same
  verses.
- `derived.diff` - the word diff of the normalised Unicode main text for every
  differing verse, not only the source-differing ones.

The `.diff` files are word-diff style, with one
`@@ BOOK CHAPTER:VERSE [category] @@` hunk and one marked line per verse,
not patchable line-based diffs: they have no line ranges and
no `-`/`+` whole-verse lines.

## Source and text

**Source** is the edition's Beta-code source tier: the official `.CCT` archive
for `rp2005`/`rp2018`, the historical `textonly-beta-code` sources for
`rp2005-2019`, and the current `data/raw/repo/rp2018-2023/ccat` for `rp2018-2023`.

**Text** is the derived Unicode accented main text in
`editions/<id>/csv/accented/no-variants/`.

**Apparatus** is the Unicode accented text with variants in
`editions/<id>/csv/accented/with-variants/`. The variant readings stay inside
literal `{...}` braces; the main text drops them.

## Notation

- `[-removed-]{+added+}` wraps changed words; unchanged text is context. The
  markers come from `difflib.SequenceMatcher` over words and whitespace.
  Beta-code apparatus braces (`{N ... }`) are part of the source text and can
  appear next to or inside the markers.
- The marker delimiters are the fixed strings `[-`, `-]`, `{+`, `+}`; a
  literal `-` or `>` next to a delimiter is part of the text (for example, a
  dash-spacing change can render as `[-εἶπεν --]{+εἶπεν-+}`).
- The Unicode Apparatus diff doubles the braces: the outer `{+`/`+}` are the
  diff markers and the inner `{...}` is the reading, so an added variant
  renders as `{+{Byz τε > δε }+}`. That is why the main text can be identical
  while the apparatus changes.
- The Text word diff is normalised: `¶` is removed, `’`/`‘`
  become `'`, and whitespace is collapsed (not removed). The exact text is in
  `changes.csv.text_left`/`text_right` and in `text.diff`.
- `@@ BOOK CHAPTER:VERSE [category] @@` opens a verse hunk. The category is
  the source-tier classification and is omitted in `derived.diff` when the
  verse is not a source-tier difference.

## Categories

The classifier applies these tests in order; the first match wins. The
`category` column is a machine-readable value: a `changes.csv` row carries
exactly one of these values, and an empty category (the identical verses) never
appears there.

| Category | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `missing` | The verse is present on one side only. | none in the current reports |
| `variant` | The apparatus reading or note changed; the main text is identical. | `1CO 3:14` in `rp2005--rp2018` |
| `apparatus-code` | Only the apparatus code letters changed; the reading is identical. | `ACT 1:15` in `rp2018--rp2018-2023` |
| `capitalization` | The main text differs only in capitalisation. | `MAT 22:37` in `rp2005--rp2005-2019` |
| `word-segmentation` | The same letters are divided into words differently. | `1CO 7:5` in `rp2005--rp2005-2019` |
| `whitespace` | Only whitespace differs. | none in the current reports |
| `punctuation` | The main text differs in punctuation (capitalisation is not considered here). | `MAT 1:18` in `rp2005-2019--rp2018` |
| `accents-breathings` | The main text differs only in accents or breathings. | `MAT 27:13` in `rp2005--rp2005-2019` |
| `letters` | The main text letters differ. | `JOH 18:11` in `rp2005--rp2018` |

`variant` and `apparatus-code` are different, and the names say how. `variant`
means the apparatus *reading or note* changed; the main text is identical.
`apparatus-code` means only the code *letter* changed; the reading is
identical. At `ACT 1:15` in `rp2018--rp2018-2023` the tag moves from `N` to `C`
and the reading is unchanged; the row is `apparatus-code`. At `1CO 3:14` in
`rp2005--rp2018` the apparatus gains the reading `{NA μένει > μενεῖ }`, so the
row is `variant`.

The code letters name these witnesses: `N` Nestle-Aland; `B` Byzantine; `C`
NA27/28; `M` ECM; `S` NA27; `E` NA28.

In the Unicode apparatus `{N` is spelled `{NA` and
`{C` is spelled `{NA27/28`, so the Beta-code change
`[-{N-]{+{C+}` renders as `[-{NA-]{+{NA27/28+}`: the same
apparatus-code change in two encodings.

`missing` and `whitespace` are defined for completeness but have no row in the
current reports. `_main_text` collapses whitespace before classifying, so a
whitespace-only difference reaches the apparatus branch and is reported as
`variant`; the `whitespace` category is kept documented rather than silently
removed.

## The `derived.diff` caveat

`derived.diff` compares the normalised main text after removing paragraph
markers (`¶`), mapping curly apostrophes (`’`/`‘`) to `'`, and
collapsing whitespace.

The source-tier comparison canonicalises dash spacing (`-` ↔ ` - `), so raw
dash-spacing differences are invisible there but survive in the derived text.
All current derived-only cases are attached-vs-spaced dashes.

Use `report.md`, `changes.csv`, `source.diff`, and `text.diff` for edition
changes; use `derived.diff` to audit everything a reader of the Unicode text
would see.

## Blank verses

LUK 17:36, ACT 8:37, ACT 15:34, and ACT 24:7 are not part of the Byzantine
tradition. Every curated edition, including `rp2005-2019`, carries them as
present empty records: empty CSV text and empty `<ab/>` TEI elements. The
source-tier comparison treats a present-empty record as a value, so an empty
verse and an absent verse are not silently equal and these four verses are in
scope like any other row.
